name: append_string_with_limit
description: Moves to the zero terminator of the destination, then appends bytes from the source until the source's zero byte is copied or the counter in the third argument runs out. If the counter ends the copy first, it writes a zero terminator after the last byte, and it returns the destination pointer.

name: compare_byte_strings_limited
description: Compares the first string with the second byte by byte and returns minus one or one at the first difference, depending on which byte is smaller. It returns zero when the strings match through the first string's terminator or until a fixed limit of about 32 thousand bytes is reached.

name: copy_zero_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from the source into the destination one at a time, including the zero terminator, and stops after that terminator. It returns the original destination pointer.

name: lookup_window_icon_fields
description: Looks up a window through a library call, follows its pointer chain to an icon entry, and stores two values from that entry into the caller's structure. The referenced text names WINDOW and icon.library, which points to window and icon handling on the Amiga.

name: format_string_into_buffer
description: Stores the destination pointer in a global slot, runs the formatting routine on the caller's arguments with a byte-writing callback, then writes a zero terminator at the next output position. It returns the formatting routine's result.

name: format_string_into_buffer_short
description: Stores the destination pointer in a global slot, runs the formatting routine on the caller's arguments with a byte-writing callback, then writes a zero terminator at the end of the output. It returns the formatting result as a 16-bit value.

name: emit_byte_to_output
description: Writes the low byte of its argument at the current output position, advances that position by one, and returns the byte. It is used as the per-character callback for the formatting routines.

name: forward_format_arguments
description: Passes its single argument on to the formatting routine, using the caller's stack arguments that follow it as the variable argument list. It returns nothing.

name: chain_two_subroutine_calls
description: A 48-instruction routine with no decompiled body; the listing only shows that it makes two subroutine calls and is called from one place. Its specific purpose cannot be determined from this evidence.

name: interpret_format_specifiers
description: Walks a format string, passing literal bytes through a character callback and expanding each percent conversion from the argument list. It handles flags, width, precision, size modifiers and the character, string, decimal, octal, unsigned and base-16 conversions, and returns the count of characters produced or minus one if the callback fails.

name: perform_signed_division
description: Works out whether the result should be negative from the signs of the two register inputs, calls a division routine, negates its result when needed, and returns it with the second input in a 64-bit pair.

name: call_and_return_concatenated
description: Calls a subroutine and returns a 64-bit value whose high half is the second register left by that call and whose low half is the second register's original value.

name: call_itself_recursively
description: Calls itself with no other work and then returns, so each invocation immediately makes another call to the same routine.

name: perform_32bit_division
description: Divides a 32-bit dividend by a 32-bit divisor, using a bit-by-bit shift and subtract loop when the divisor is wider than 16 bits and a 16-bit division otherwise. It returns the quotient and remainder as a 64-bit pair.

name: compute_string_length
description: Walks forward from the given pointer to the zero terminator without changing memory, and returns the number of bytes before that terminator.

name: forward_call_no_arguments
description: Calls one subroutine with no arguments and returns without a value. It is referenced by address from one other routine.

name: invoke_three_subroutines
description: A 21-instruction routine that makes three subroutine calls and is referenced from three other routines and by address. No decompiled body is available, so its specific effect is not described.

name: return_without_effect
description: Its decompiled body is a bare return with no operations, and it is referenced by address from one caller. The listing shows no visible effect.

name: invoke_two_subroutines
description: A 15-instruction routine that makes two subroutine calls and is referenced by two other routines and by address. No decompiled body is available, so its specific effect is not described.

name: emit_structure_byte_output
description: Writes the byte at a fixed offset of the structure held in one address register to the current output position, advances that position by one, and returns the byte.

name: visit_fixed_size_records
description: Walks a table of 22-byte records from a fixed start address up to a fixed end address, calling a per-record routine on each record in turn.

name: release_record_resources
description: Returns an all-ones error value when given no record; otherwise, for a record with its active flag set, calls helper routines selected by the flag bits, combines their results, then clears the record's three words and flag byte and returns the combined result.

name: release_record_without_null_check
description: Takes its record from an address register and performs the same flag-driven helper calls and record clearing as the null-checked variant, without the null test.

name: write_byte_into_buffer
description: Writes the byte from its argument into a small buffered output record, calling a helper to set up the buffer when none exists and marking an error when a write fails. It returns the byte written, zero after a reset request, or an all-ones error value.

name: write_parameter_byte_to_buffer
description: Writes the byte at a fixed offset of its parameter block into the same buffered output record and returns it. When the sentinel field in the parameter block is minus one, it resets the record instead.

name: emit_parameter_byte_buffered
description: Resets the record when its sentinel field is minus one; otherwise writes the parameter byte directly, or through a helper when the element size is one. A failed helper marks the record as errored and the routine returns an all-ones error value.

name: emit_parameter_byte_direct
description: Writes the parameter block byte into the output record, using a helper for single-byte element sizes and marking the record as errored if that helper fails. It does not perform the sentinel reset check.

name: write_byte_and_advance_buffer
description: Sets the output pointer to the start of the buffer, marks the record as active, stores the parameter byte there and advances the pointer by one. It returns the byte in its low position.

name: find_free_record_slot
description: Scans the table of 22-byte records for one whose flag byte is clear, zeroes its three words, and returns its address, or a null pointer when every record is in use.

name: find_next_free_record
description: From the record address in a register, scans forward through the 22-byte table for a record with a clear flag byte, zeroes its three words, and returns its address, or null at the end of the table.

name: clear_record_header_words
description: Zeroes the first three 32-bit words of the record in an address register and returns, leaving the flag byte unchanged.

name: initialize_stream_buffer
description: Sets up an output record: if the helper returns no buffer, it records a size of one and points the buffer at an inline slot; otherwise it stores the supplied buffer, a 1024-byte size and flag bits, and sets a further flag when a second helper reports success.

name: setup_buffered_stream_record
description: Stores a 1024-byte size and a buffer flag bit in the record, takes the buffer pointer from the caller's frame, and sets another flag when a helper reports success.

name: release_all_list_nodes
description: Walks a singly linked list from a global head pointer, calling a release helper on each node with the node's payload address, then clears the head and returns zero.

name: release_list_nodes_from_pointer
description: Walks a linked list starting at the node in an address register, releasing each node through a helper call, then clears the list head and returns zero. The first node is always processed.

name: allocate_and_link_list_node
description: Calls an allocation helper for a block sized from its argument plus eight, returning null on failure. On success it links the new node at the head of a global list, stores the caller's pointer in it, and returns the address after the two link words.

name: push_list_node_with_payload
description: Pushes a node onto the head of a global linked list, storing the previous head and a payload pointer taken from the caller's frame, and returns the address after the two link words.

name: forward_low_word_argument
description: Passes the low sixteen bits of its argument to a subroutine and returns nothing.

name: remove_list_node_by_payload
description: Searches the global list for the node whose payload address matches the argument, unlinks it, and releases it through a helper using its stored size. It returns zero when the node is found and minus one when no node matches.

name: unlink_frame_node_from_list
description: Walks the list from the head register looking for the node whose payload matches the pointer in the caller's frame, unlinks it, and releases it through a helper. It returns zero on success and minus one if the node is absent.

name: unlink_list_node
description: Unlinks the node in an address register from a singly linked list by pointing its predecessor, or the list head when there is none, at the node's successor. It then calls a helper and returns zero.

name: pop_list_head_node
description: Sets the list head to the successor of the node in an address register, calls a helper, and returns zero.

name: check_table_entry_status
description: Checks that the index argument falls inside the table and that its six-byte entry is populated. On a bad index it stores an error code of 2 and returns an all-ones value; otherwise it returns one when the helper succeeds for that entry and zero when it does not.

name: check_handle_is_interactive
description: Looks up the table entry selected by the index in the caller's frame and asks the DOS IsInteractive wrapper whether the handle stored there is interactive, returning true when it is.

name: return_zero_constant
description: Returns zero without any other work and is referenced by address from one other routine.

name: delete_file_recording_error
description: Calls the DeleteFile wrapper on the argument and, when that call fails, stores the DOS error code from the IoErr wrapper in the error slot and returns minus one. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: return_zero_value_only
description: Returns zero without any other work and is referenced by address from one other routine.

name: dispatch_two_helper_calls
description: A 19-instruction routine that makes two helper calls and is called from five places. No decompiled body was produced, so its exact behaviour is not described.

name: check_mode_flags_then_call
description: Checks that the low two flag bits of a structure field are set; if not, it stores an error code of 5 and returns minus one. Otherwise it calls a helper with two caller-frame fields and, when that helper fails, stores the error code from a second helper and returns minus one.

name: write_buffer_recording_error
description: Calls the Write wrapper with a buffer, length and handle taken from the caller's frame. On failure it stores the DOS error code from the IoErr wrapper and returns minus one; otherwise it returns the write result.

name: return_empty_callback
description: Contains only a return with no operations and is referenced by address from one caller.

name: poll_mask_bit_result
description: Calls a library function with zero and a fixed mask, and if that mask bit is set it returns the returned mask when a global option is zero. Otherwise it calls a helper and returns zero.

name: call_helper_return_zero
description: Calls a helper with no arguments and then returns zero.

name: write_fixed_block_then_callback
description: Writes a four-byte block at a fixed address through the Write wrapper, passes the result to a helper, then calls a second helper with no arguments.

name: invoke_optional_callback_then_helper
description: Calls an optional callback held in a global slot when one is set, then calls a helper with no arguments and returns.

name: tear_down_entry_tables
description: Releases a table of six-byte entries by calling a helper on each entry and then on the table block. It then runs an optional callback, releases three further saved resources, and makes an optional library call through the exec supervisor before returning the value held on the stack.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, sits in a gap that decodes as code, and is not called in the reference run.

name: release_table_entry_by_index
description: Validates the index against the table count and checks whether the six-byte entry is populated. On a bad index it stores an error code of 2 and returns minus one. Otherwise it releases the entry's resource unless its flag bit marks it as not owned, clears the entry and returns zero.

name: close_dos_file_handle
description: Calls the DOS library's Close function through the library base stored in a global slot. It returns nothing.

name: call_dos_current_dir
description: Calls the DOS library's CurrentDir function through the library base stored in a global slot and returns nothing.

name: call_dos_input_function
description: Calls the DOS library's Input function through the library base stored in a global slot and returns nothing.

name: call_dos_open_function
description: Calls the DOS library's Open function through the library base stored in a global slot and returns nothing.

name: call_dos_output_function
description: Calls the DOS library's Output function through the library base stored in a global slot and returns nothing.

name: call_library_entry_108
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 108 from the library base held in a global slot and returns nothing. The listing does not name that library, so the function's purpose is not described.

name: call_library_entry_450
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 450 from the library base held in a global slot and returns nothing. The listing does not name that library, so the function's purpose is not described.

name: forward_to_library_entry_414
description: Makes one call to the library function at offset minus 414 from the library base held in a global slot, then returns. The listing does not name that library, so the function's purpose is not described.

name: call_library_entry_414
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 414 from the library base held in a global slot and returns nothing. The listing does not name that library, so the function's purpose is not described.

description: Calls the library function at offset minus 198 from the library base held in a global slot and returns nothing. The listing does not name that library, so the function's purpose is not described.

description: Calls the library function at offset minus 294 from the library base held in a global slot and returns nothing. The listing does not name that library, so the function's purpose is not described.

description: Makes one call to the library function at offset minus 210 from the library base held in a global slot, then returns. The listing does not name that library, so the function's purpose is not described.

name: call_library_entry_210
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 210 from the library base held in a global slot and returns nothing. The listing does not name that library, so the function's purpose is not described.

description: Calls the library function at offset minus 336 from the library base held in a global slot and returns nothing. The listing does not name that library, so the function's purpose is not described.

name: call_library_entry_372
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 372 from the library base held in a global slot and returns nothing. The listing does not name that library, so the function's purpose is not described.

name: call_library_entry_444
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 444 from the library base held in a global slot and returns nothing. The listing does not name that library, so the function's purpose is not described.

name: forward_to_library_entry_552
description: Makes one call to the library function at offset minus 552 from the library base held in a global slot, then returns. It is reached from the boot entry routine, and the listing does not name the library function.

name: call_library_entry_552
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 552 from the library base held in a global slot and returns nothing. The listing does not name that library, so the function's purpose is not described.

name: call_library_entry_366
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 366 from the library base held in a global slot and returns nothing. The listing does not name that library, so the function's purpose is not described.

name: call_library_entry_378
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 378 from the library base held in a global slot and returns nothing. The listing does not name that library, so the function's purpose is not described.

name: forward_to_single_callee
description: A one-instruction routine that makes a single subroutine call and returns. The decompiler produced no body, so the callee is not identified.

name: stub_empty_no_instructions
description: The listing reports zero instructions at this location, so it contains no code of its own. The decompiler produced no body, and it is called from two places.

name: initialize_hardware_at_entry
description: Program entry routine that disables multitasking around opening graphics.library through the exec library calls. It then builds copper, bitplane and blitter data in memory and writes the custom chip registers controlling the blitter, copper, DMA and interrupts. The referenced text includes graphics.library and a string named glorious.

name: service_fire_button_interrupt
description: Interrupt-style handler reached through a vector stored in data. It checks a counter global and calls helpers, sets a flag when the fire-button line in the CIA port register is clear, and writes a status value. The listing says that port carries the fire buttons and disk status and that the interrupt request register is touched.

name: advance_ring_indices_and_accumulate
description: Advances two ring-buffer offsets and recomputes two stored values from table entries shifted right by nine bits. When a stored counter exceeds 200 it subtracts 30 and adds a 32-bit quotient and remainder of 5000 divided by that counter into an accumulator; otherwise it sets a flag.

name: initialize_tables_with_stride
description: Fills a 31-entry table of 32-bit values that rise by 680 per step, then makes helper calls. It clears a 98-entry word table and calls two helpers for each entry, with eight further helper calls in between.

name: reset_tables_with_stride
description: Has the same body as the initialisation routine at the neighbouring address: fills a 31-entry table with a 680 step, makes helper calls, then clears a 98-entry word table with helper calls for each entry.

name: rotate_three_buffer_pointers
description: Rotates three stored buffer pointers, updates a pointer pair, then waits while a status bit in one structure is set. It finishes by writing size and control fields into that structure.

name: advance_position_and_fill_pointers
description: Advances a counter and, when the counter reaches seven, sets a flag instead. Otherwise it updates a stored position and rate, and when the position passes 237 it steps the counter and recomputes the rate by dividing. It then writes the two halves of an address into each of four eight-byte entries, with the address rising by four each time.

name: set_status_and_refresh_entries
description: Sets the high bit of a status byte held in an address register, advances a ring index, and refreshes eight entries. For each entry it computes a table-derived offset, stores two address halves and copies three words from a lookup table into the entry's fields.

name: refresh_entries_with_status_set
description: Has the same body as the neighbouring routine: sets the high bit of a status byte, advances a ring index, and refreshes eight entries from the lookup table.

name: refresh_entries_without_status
description: Refreshes the same eight entries from the lookup table without setting the status bit. The listing reports a touch of the custom chip block.

name: refresh_entries_single_lookup
description: Refreshes eight entries from the lookup table, storing address halves and copying three lookup words into each entry's trailing fields. It does not set the status bit.

name: wait_then_program_blitter
description: Waits until the blitter-busy bit in the DMA status register is clear, then writes control and mask words and two address fields into the chip register block. The offsets fit blitter registers, but the listing does not name them.

name: program_blitter_and_copy_block
description: Waits for the blitter-busy bit to clear, writes control and mask words, then copies a run of table values into a memory region at descending offsets. The listing also notes a comparison with AmigaDOS hunk type codes, which the decompiled body does not show.

name: copy_table_block_unrolled
description: A 314-instruction routine whose visible part copies a long run of 32-bit values from one table into another at descending offsets, and the listing reports a custom chip touch. The pseudo-code is cut off partway, so the rest of its behaviour is not described.

name: transform_triplets_to_points
description: Advances three ring-buffer indices, reads table entries at those indices and builds several fixed-point coefficients from pairs of them. It then applies those coefficients to each three-value entry, divides by a computed depth value, and stores a pair of 16-bit results.

name: compute_face_shade_entries
description: Waits until the blitter-busy bit is clear, then sets fields in the chip register block. It walks a list of records ending in a negative value, computes a signed area term from three coordinate pairs, and when that term selects a record it stores a looked-up entry clamped at 50; otherwise it skips ahead in the list.

name: store_clamped_face_values
description: Waits until the blitter-busy bit clears, sets the same chip register fields as its neighbouring routine, then walks the record list. For records chosen by a signed area test it stores a clamped value, doubled, into a table; otherwise it skips ahead in the list.

name: clip_and_setup_line_draw
description: Orders two endpoints and clips the segment against two horizontal limits using interpolated intersections. It then computes octant and step terms for the line and writes them, with start and step values, to blitter-style chip registers, repeating the values with an offset when a flag bit is set.

name: clip_and_setup_line_unmasked
description: Performs the same clipping and line-term calculation as its neighbouring routine, but takes the endpoint values without the low-bit masking. It writes the results to the same blitter-style chip registers.

name: setup_unclipped_line_draw
description: Orders two endpoints without any clipping, computes the octant and step terms of the line, and writes them to blitter-style chip registers. It repeats the start and step values with an offset when a flag bit is set.

name: fill_words_from_helper
description: Loops over a count held in a data register, calling a helper on each step and storing its word result at the address held in an address register, then returns.

name: store_helper_words_in_loop
description: Loops a count from a data register, calling a helper on each pass and storing its word result at the address held in an address register.

name: copy_word_then_fill_loop
description: Copies one word from the source address register to the destination, then loops a count, calling a helper on each pass and storing its word result at the destination.

name: fill_word_pairs_from_helper
description: Loops a count, calling a helper on each pass and writing its word result into two consecutive words at the address register.

name: duplicate_word_pair_fill
description: Has the same body as the neighbouring routine: loops a count, calling a helper and writing its word result into two consecutive words at the address register.

name: step_three_nibbles_toward_target
description: Splits a 12-bit value into three four-bit fields and moves each field one step toward its corresponding target value held in other registers. It returns the recombined value.

name: accumulate_pairs_and_set_bits
description: On the first call with a zero flag it initialises a pair table. It then adds delta pairs into that table over sixteen passes, ORing a bit into a memory byte at each computed address, and issues blitter-style register sequences. A stored offset advances by 368 per call and wraps at a limit, when a byte stream is reloaded.

name: advance_offset_and_reload_stream
description: Advances a stored offset by 368 and, when it passes its limit, resets it and reads a fresh byte stream. It then issues a short run of blitter-style register sequences; the listing also reports a touch of the CIA B port register.

name: compute_scaled_pair_differences
description: Walks two paired tables of 32-bit values and stores the shifted-right-by-four difference of each pair in a destination table. The loop count comes from a data register.

name: recompute_scaled_pair_differences
description: Has the same body as the neighbouring routine: stores the shifted-right-by-four differences of paired table values into a destination table, with the loop count taken from a data register.

name: decode_byte_stream_into_entries
description: Reads a byte stream until a zero byte. Bytes with the high bit set are dispatched through a jump table, while other bytes are expanded into bit-position entries, stopping after 2000 entries. It then copies the collected pairs into a destination table and sets a completion flag.

name: clear_init_flag
description: Clears a global flag that marks the pair table as initialised, then returns. It is reached through a pointer stored in the data area.

name: load_next_text_glyph_columns
description: Once every sixteen calls it reads the next text byte, converting values above 96 to uppercase by subtracting 32, and fills three buffers of 14 entries from a character table. On every call it issues three blitter-style copies of those buffers at fixed offsets.

name: reset_pointer_list_after_scan
description: Scans a byte table for the first entry above a running threshold. When the scan completes it clears a 30-entry pointer list, points each slot into a block, sets status bits and clears several state globals. The listing reports a touch of the CIA A port register, but the visible code does not read it.

name: advance_audio_tick_state
description: Advances a tick counter, and on the wrap runs a short delay and writes eight pointer words into the custom chip audio channel registers. Between wraps it calls a helper, and it steps an accumulator by 16 per tick, cycling a byte index and wrapping it at a stored length once the accumulator reaches 1024.

name: update_audio_channel_effects
description: Calls four helpers, then reads a command word and branches on its low nibble. Depending on the command it slides a stored position, selects a table value by a counter modulo three, scales a level, or stores a parameter, then writes results to a state word. The listing reports writes to the four audio channel location registers.

name: process_tracker_channel_row
description: Reads a packed command word for one channel when its state is empty, then loads a sample pointer, length, volume and period from tables for a non-zero instrument. It applies the row's effect and writes the channel's location, length and volume registers, and the listing also shows the DMA control register. The structure resembles a music-tracker channel step.

name: apply_tracker_effect_command
description: Applies one effect command to a channel state. Depending on the command's low nibble it slides a period value, selects a table value by a counter modulo three, applies a table-driven offset, or stores a parameter, and it writes the resulting value to the channel's register block.

name: copy_channel_word_to_register
description: Copies one 16-bit field from a channel state record into a register-block field and returns. The field offsets are fixed.

name: find_target_period_entry
description: Searches a per-instrument table of 16-bit period values for the first entry above the channel's current period, stepping back one entry when a flag bit is set. It stores that entry as the target value and sets a direction flag depending on whether the current value is above it.

name: slide_channel_value_toward_target
description: Moves a stored channel value toward its target by a per-tick increment, clearing the target once it is reached. It then looks up a table entry for the current value and writes the result to a register-block field, returning the combined value.

name: apply_waveform_offset_to_register
description: Computes an offset from a phase counter using one of three waveform modes selected by two bits: a table lookup, a signed ramp, or a constant. It scales the offset by a depth nibble, applies its sign, adds it to a base value, advances the phase by a rate nibble, and writes the result to a register-block field.

name: interpret_channel_effect_code
description: Calls a helper, then reads the low nibble of a channel command byte as an effect code. Depending on the code it slides a stored position, selects a table value, scales a level, or stores a parameter, and returns the resulting value. The listing reports a touch of the CIA A port register, which the visible code does not read.

name: store_low_nibble_parameter
description: Copies the low four bits of a parameter byte into a state byte of the channel record and returns.

name: run_program_entry_sequence
description: Program entry routine that calls a helper and compares its result with 31. On a match it checks a stored flag and copies a block of bytes into a memory region before calling into it; otherwise it stores the result and makes two helper calls.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler produced only a halt marker for this location, so it is bad data rather than a routine. It has no behaviour to describe and is referenced by address from one place.

name: return_zero_handler_value
description: Returns zero without any other work. It is referenced as a handler pointer from the data area.

name: return_zero_callback_value
description: Returns zero without any other work. It is referenced as a pointer from the data area.

name: return_empty_handler
description: Contains only a return with no operations. It is referenced as a handler pointer from the data area.

name: clear_state_and_run_setup
description: Clears a run of 91 bytes in a structure, then runs a chain of helpers that stop at the first failure. When a flag bit is set it calls the intuition library's CloseWorkBench through a library vector, and it returns zero when every step succeeds.

name: open_workbench_when_flagged
description: Calls three helpers, then calls the intuition library's OpenWorkBench through a library vector when a flag bit is set. It runs one more helper and returns the register value unchanged.

name: probe_dos_file_handle
description: Opens a file through the DOS library and, when the handle is valid, passes it to a second DOS call before closing it. It returns zero on success and the error value 33 when the open fails or the second call reports a negative result.

name: parse_hunk_records_into_buffer
description: Walks AmigaDOS hunk records, returning at once unless the first word is the header type. For a code record it copies the record's longs into the destination, skips relocation records by their stored count, and stops at the end record.

name: load_hunk_code_records
description: Walks AmigaDOS hunk records, skipping relocation records by their stored count and copying code record contents into the destination. It stops when it reaches a record type it does not handle.

name: return_empty_gap_routine
description: Contains only a return with no operations. It sits in a gap that decodes as code and is called from one place.

name: copy_counted_long_block
description: Reads a count from the first long of a source block, then copies that many longs following it into the destination pointer. It returns the register value unchanged.

name: scan_hunk_and_copy_code
description: Walks hunk records by their stored lengths until it reaches a code record, then copies that record's longs into the destination. It stops at the end record, or when a record type is neither code nor relocation.

name: apply_relocation_offsets
description: For a relocation record it adds a base value to each longword at the offsets listed in the record, looping over the stored count. It does nothing for other record types.

name: return_stack_value_unchanged
description: Returns the value taken from the stack without changing it, so it has no effect. It sits in a gap that decodes as code and is called from two places.

name: return_stack_value_passthrough
description: Returns the value taken from the stack without changing it, so it has no effect. It sits in a gap that decodes as code and is called from two places.

name: run_three_checks_then_cleanup
description: Calls a helper, and if it returns zero calls a second helper and then a third. When all three return zero it returns; otherwise it calls two cleanup helpers before returning.

name: own_blitter_and_forbid
description: Calls the graphics library's OwnBlitter through a vector in the caller's structure, then calls exec's Forbid through the exec base held in a global slot.

name: permit_and_disown_blitter
description: Calls exec's Permit through the exec base held in a global slot, then calls the graphics library's DisownBlitter through a vector in the caller's structure. It returns the register value unchanged.

name: reset_custom_chip_registers
description: Disables interrupts through the Disable wrapper, writes clear masks and reset values to interrupt, DMA and colour registers, and zeroes a block of 32 colour words. It then calls through a jump table the decompiler could not recover.

name: reset_cia_and_custom_registers
description: Writes interrupt and DMA reset values through the custom chip base register, zeroes a block of 32 words, and then calls through a jump table the decompiler could not recover. The listing reports a touch of both CIA interrupt control registers.

name: display_intuition_beep
description: Calls the intuition library's DisplayBeep through a vector in the caller's structure and returns the register value unchanged.

name: write_string_to_dos_stream
description: Measures a zero-terminated string and returns error code 15 when it is empty. Otherwise it writes the string through the DOS Write vector, then makes a second write call, returning 16 if the first fails, 24 if the second fails, and zero when both succeed.

name: write_counted_pair_checked
description: Returns error code 15 when the count argument is zero. Otherwise it makes two calls through the DOS Write vector, returning 16 if the first fails, 24 if the second fails, and zero when both succeed.

name: write_two_chunks_checked
description: Makes two calls through the DOS Write vector, returning 16 if the first fails, 24 if the second fails, and zero when both succeed.

name: write_one_chunk_checked
description: Makes one call through the DOS Write vector and returns 24 when it fails, or zero when it succeeds.

name: return_stack_value_callback
description: Returns the value taken from the stack without changing it, so it has no effect. It is referenced as a pointer from the data area and called from three places.

name: store_request_and_autorequest
description: Saves a word from the caller's structure and a second argument into global slots, then calls the intuition library's AutoRequest through a vector in that structure. It returns the register value unchanged.

name: call_autorequest_directly
description: Calls the intuition library's AutoRequest through a vector in the caller's structure and returns its result.

name: show_alert_when_nonzero
description: When its argument is nonzero, calls the intuition library's DisplayAlert through a vector in the caller's structure. Otherwise it does nothing.

name: validate_size_arguments
description: Returns error code 21 when the second argument is zero or negative, zero when the first argument is below 42, and error code 22 otherwise. The referenced text is a message about failing to open graphics.library, which this code does not use.

name: poll_task_message_port
description: Calls exec's FindTask, and if a field of the returned task is zero it calls FindTask again and then GetMsg. It stores the message in the caller's structure when a pointer is present and returns zero.

name: poll_task_message_queue
description: Calls exec's FindTask, and if a field of the returned task is zero it calls FindTask again and then GetMsg. It stores the message in the caller's structure when a pointer is present and returns zero.

name: poll_task_message_slot
description: Calls exec's FindTask, and if a field of the returned task is zero it calls FindTask again and then GetMsg. It stores the message in the caller's structure when a pointer is present and returns zero.

name: open_three_libraries
description: Opens three libraries through exec's OpenLibrary, storing each base in the caller's structure. It returns error codes 1, 2 or 3 for the first library that fails to open. When a flag is clear it also calls the DOS Output function and returns 4 if that gives no handle, otherwise zero.

name: close_three_libraries
description: Calls exec's CloseLibrary on each of up to three stored library bases and clears each stored pointer. It returns nothing.

name: open_misc_resource_and_setup
description: Opens the misc resource through exec's OpenResource, storing it and returning error 4 when that fails. Otherwise it runs three helpers and returns the last helper's result. The referenced text includes misc.resource and serial.device.

name: allocate_misc_resources
description: Claims two misc resources through the first entry of the misc resource vector, recording each claim in a flag byte. It returns error 5 or 6 when a claim fails, and zero when both succeed.

name: claim_misc_resource_pair
description: Claims two misc resources through the first entry of the misc resource vector, recording each claim in a flag byte. It returns error 27 or 28 when a claim fails, and zero when both succeed.

name: allocate_potgo_resource
description: Opens potgo.resource through exec's OpenResource and returns error 7 when it is missing. Otherwise it disables multitasking, allocates pot bits through the resource's first entry, records the result, and re-enables multitasking. It returns zero when the result matches the expected mask, and otherwise the value from a further helper call.

name: run_three_setup_helpers
description: Calls three helpers in sequence and returns, with no checks on their results.

name: free_misc_resources
description: For each misc resource whose claim flag byte is set, calls the resource's release entry at offset minus 12 and clears the flag.

name: free_misc_resource_pair
description: Releases two misc resources through the release entry at offset minus 12 for each claim flag byte that is set, clearing each flag as it goes.

name: free_potgo_bits
description: When the potgo claim value is nonzero, clears it and calls the potgo resource's release entry at offset minus 12.

name: remove_named_device_if_present
description: Disables multitasking, looks up a named node with exec's FindName, removes it with RemDevice when it is found, and then re-enables multitasking.

name: install_interrupt_servers
description: Copies three stored values from the caller's structure and removes an existing interrupt server through exec when one is set. It then adds further interrupt servers through a library call at offset minus six, returning error 29 or 30 when one of those calls fails and zero otherwise.

name: remove_interrupt_servers_and_release
description: Removes an interrupt server through exec's RemIntServer when its flag is set, then calls exec's entry at offset minus 12 for two further flagged blocks. It clears each flag after acting on it.

name: allocate_optional_memory_block
description: When the size field of the caller's structure is nonzero, allocates a memory block through exec's AllocMem and stores the pointer. It returns error 32 when the allocation is null, and otherwise passes control on to a helper.

name: allocate_memory_then_continue
description: Has the same body as the neighbouring allocation routine: allocates a memory block through exec's AllocMem when a size field is nonzero, returns error 32 on a null result, and otherwise passes control to a helper.

name: setup_buffers_with_checks
description: Calls helpers to fill pointer fields of the structure when its size fields are nonzero. It returns error 35 or 37 when one of those helpers fails, and error 31 when no earlier check fails.

name: find_region_with_free_size
description: Walks the list of memory regions from a global root and returns the free size of the first region whose attribute flags match and that is large enough for the requested size. It returns minus one when no region matches.

name: record_memory_stats_and_allocate
description: Records four values from exec's AvailMem into the caller's structure, then allocates optional blocks through AllocMem. It returns error 11 or 12 when the first allocation attempts fail, and otherwise continues with further allocations.

name: allocate_three_optional_blocks
description: Allocates up to three optional blocks through AllocMem, storing each pointer and returning error 12, 13 or 14 for the first allocation that fails. It returns zero when all requested blocks are allocated.

name: allocate_two_optional_blocks
description: Allocates up to two optional blocks through AllocMem, storing each pointer and returning error 13 or 14 when one fails. It returns zero otherwise.

name: allocate_final_optional_block
description: Allocates one optional block through AllocMem when its size field is nonzero, storing the pointer and returning error 14 when it is null. It returns zero otherwise.

name: free_five_memory_blocks
description: Frees up to five stored memory blocks through exec's FreeMem, clearing each stored pointer after it is released.

name: fill_eight_byte_record_words
description: Loops over a count, writing a word into the second field of each eight-byte record starting at the address held in an address register, then returns.
